title: Slugs are human-readable, mutable, unique within parent scope only
context: Identifiers must be memorable and readable; globally unique slugs would collide across projects and prevent natural naming in different contexts.
decision: Every node carries a `slug` field as a human-readable string, unique only within its parent scope (e.g., within a service, within a module, within the screen collection). Slug is mutable; `id` is immutable. When a user renames a node, the slug changes but the `id` stays the same.
consequences: Identifiers can be natural and readable; no global collision risk; rename operations do not break references because they use `id`; slug scope rules must be enforced by the linter.
